correctness.rationale: Standard shifted Jacobi contiguous relation q=p-(1-t)r and derivative p_prime=(k+beta+1)r, together with the Jacobi differential equation, yield a first-order system for q,r and the exact differentiated boundary identity. Integrating from 0 gives the factorization, and Jacobi orthogonality normalizes each energy to 1 at t=1. At each zero z_j of p, R(z_j)=-z_j(1-z_j)r(z_j)^2<0; at derivative zeros c_j R(c_j)=p(c_j)^2>0; endpoint values are positive for beta>-1. The resulting 2k alternating intervals force 2k distinct interior roots, and deg R=2k proves exhaustiveness and simplicity. Special k=0 separately yields t^(beta+1)(1-t)>0. Fresh independent symbolic checks at 24 rational (k,beta) combinations reproduced the differentiated identity, integral factorization and 2k simple root brackets. This is an analytic all-real-parameter zero count, not inferred from numerical root searches.
residual_risks: No assertion about arbitrary apertures, multi-mode compressed disk operators or equal-total-degree mode pairs.
The proof relies on standard real-beta Jacobi zero theorems, not a newly proved universal interlacing theorem.

value.rationale: The full 2k crossing count is a nontrivial shape theorem for naturally normalized radial-energy distributions of Zernike modes. It gives precise alternating energy-order reversals and locations relative to all radial nodes, contrasting with the separate fixed-total-degree tangency phenomenon. The invariant is intrinsically relevant to disk-mode localization; no multi-mode theorem is required.
residual_risks: This is a single-mode centered-disk/ball comparison, not an assertion about aperture noise or joint modal spectra.

final_claim: For k>=1 and any real beta>-1, normalized Jacobi cumulative energies E_(k,beta) and E_(k,beta+1) differ by t^(beta+1)(1-t)[P_k^(0,beta+1)(2t-1)^2-(1-t)P_(k-1)^(1,beta+1)(2t-1)^2], whose polynomial has exactly 2k distinct simple interior zeros. The two energies cross and reverse sign at each; k=0 has no crossing. Positions interleave the k radial nodes and k-1 turning points.
limitations: Covers beta>-1 and shifts exactly beta to beta+1 with same k; k=0 handled separately.
